subject: Interleaved metering timestamps causing payout delta (AWS/GCP/Azure)

Cc: GCP Marketplace Support <gcp-marketplace-support@google.com>, AWS Marketplace Merchant Support <aws-marketplace-merchant-support@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Interleaved timestamp / payout mismatch for Oct usage

Hi Rafael,

We're seeing a $42,350 net payout shortfall on our Oct marketplace remittance. Your gross usage numbers match our invoices for the most part, but the settlement credits applied across AWS vs GCP look inconsistent — specifically entries where the GCP usage rows have timestamps that appear to have been rounded back by one hour and then attributed to a different billing window. That shift is triggering a cross-marketplace offset on our ledger.

I've attached a minimal export showing the GCP rows we think were reclassified (gcp_usage_export_2028-10.csv). Can you confirm whether Redwood applies any timezone normalization or daylight-saving adjustments when merging incoming metering events from marketplace feeds?

We need to get a reconciliation for our accounting close next week. If you prefer, we can hop on a quick screen-share; our finance ops are available Monday morning UTC+8.

Thanks,
Maya Shen
Director, Revenue Ops
CloudWave Inc.

Subject: Re: Interleaved timestamp / payout mismatch for Oct usage

Thanks Maya — and sorry for the disruption. Tagging internal folks: Jonas (finance systems), Naomi (partner payouts), Camila (platform telemetry).

Short answer: Redwood ingests per-event metering from each marketplace and stores timestamps in UTC. We do have a post-ingest normalization step for vendor-provided timestamps that are detected as non-UTC or missing tz metadata; that step attempts to infer timezone when explicit tz data isn't present, and it may fall back to the marketplace-provided account timezone in rare cases. That heuristic has been tightened this year but we've rolled a change in late Oct to tolerate small deltas which—if combined with interleaving across marketplaces—can reassign a row to the prior hourly bucket.

Jonas / Naomi / Camila — can you review Maya's sample and confirm whether the Oct 29-31 ingestion pipeline logged any timezone-normalization warnings? If we did mutate timestamps, we should provide the original raw events for audit.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Marketplace Finance Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Interleaved timestamp / payout mismatch for Oct usage

Rafael — quick update from the pipeline logs.

- We observed a spike of ~1.2M metering events on Oct 30 23:00-00:30 UTC from one GCP feed tied to the CloudWave project id.
- In ~0.4% of those events, the vendor timestamp field was provided as a naive local time (no tz). Our fallback logic used the feed account timezone (Asia/Singapore) which shifted those rows to UTC+8 during ingest.
- Later, when we merged marketplace feeds for aggregate windows, our windowing job (hour_bucketer v2) applied a -1 hour correction for a subset of events flagged as probable DST-carryover; that was a conservative attempt to avoid double-counting for feeds that replay older events. That correction appears to be what moved some rows into the previous hour bucket and consequently changed settlement grouping across marketplaces.

I've attached the raw ingest snapshot (evidence_packet_CloudWave.zip) and a short query result referencing the affected event ids. I recommend we:
1) Provide CloudWave the raw ingest rows plus the post-normalization rows for audit.
2) Re-run the hour_bucketer v2 for Oct 30 with DST-carryover disabled and compare totals.
3) If that restores parity, issue an adjusting credit memo and include a note in the next payout cycle.

I'll queue a re-run and surface diffs by EOD PST.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Finance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 07:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Interleaved timestamp / payout mismatch for Oct usage

Maya — attaching what Jonas pulled from the ingest layer. We ran the re-bucketing job with DST-carryover off and the delta reconciles $41,980 of the $42,350 you reported. There remains a $370 difference which looks like an unrelated AWS rounding/fee allocation.

What I'm sending: 
- evidence_packet_CloudWave.zip (raw ingest rows + post-normalization rows)
- gcp_usage_export_2028-10.csv (your sample)
- aws_invoices_q3_2028.pdf (merchant statement showing fee lines we suspect)

Next steps proposed:
1) If CloudWave confirms the raw rows match your exports, we will prepare an adjusting credit for $41,980 in the next payout cycle and include an itemized reconciliation.
2) For the remaining $370 we will coordinate with AWS merchant support to clarify fee allocation (cc'd).
3) We will backfill a permanent telemetry flag to mark naive timestamps and surface them to partners prior to settlement.

Would you like us to open a joint ticket with GCP and AWS for the remaining AWS-specific fee carve? If so, we can include the relevant event ids and timeline (JIRA-BILL-879).

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Marketplace Finance Lead | Redwood Inference
